caption: The drawing is a technical illustration composed of various garment pattern pieces arranged on a light-colored background. Each component is outlined with thin, precise black lines and accompanied by alphanumeric labels and annotations. The largest pieces are two trapezoidal shapes labeled “CENTER FRONT” and “CENTER BACK,” each with dashed lines and additional notations. Multiple smaller shapes are distributed above these, including rectangles, curved pieces, and a diamond, each labeled with letters such as A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, and J, some with numbers in parentheses to indicate multiples. Edge details and seam placements are indicated by dashed or dotted lines. A long, narrow rectangle at the top is labeled E, while a similarly shaped piece at the bottom is labeled F. To the right, a rectangular area labeled “SCALE 1/8"” appears alongside a scale ruler. In the lower part of the drawing, a block of text in all capital letters explains the function of each labeled piece and describes how the garment is assembled, specifying where sections join or reinforce one another, how edging is applied, and locations for eyelets and drawstrings. The entire composition is neat, free of shading, and rendered entirely in monochrome line work.
title: Shift: pattern
